title: Chapter 5: Beyond the Lines
notes: CH05 expanded finale v2.1 (owner review draft; dialogue proposed). Scene 01: Hale's inspection briefing and team pass. Scene 02: two recordings of the former treatment room door, preserved as unresolved; nobody opens the door. Scenes 03-04: records review and the analyst's report (a supernatural-mechanism conclusion is sent back for revision). Scene 05: Bennett's patient-care follow-up, escalated generically (no case findings). Scene 06: shared sources are not counted twice. Scene 07: three responsible endings (independent review, restricted access, continuing inquiry); delaying the report is refused. Scene 08 (owner approved the screenplay text): Mara asks about the records review; the answer stays within what is established, and suggesting the records explain her health is refused. No clinical state changes. Scenes 09-10: ending epilogue, then rounds with Bennett. The game's supernatural truth stays out of the professional record and every clinical chart.

objectives.text: Hale is briefing the return inspection. Find him at Interview Room A's door.
Collect the team pass from Hale.
Go down with the team to the Ward Zero observation room.
Bring everyone back and return the team pass to Hale.
The records historian's notes are on the Records worksheet.
The independent analyst's report is at the office workstation.
Bennett needs you for something that doesn't involve the basement.
The four-source comparison is on the Records worksheet.
Mara Ellis has asked to see you in Interview Room A.
Bennett is at the nursing station.

staff_lines.text: Every person accounted for. Every exit checked.
And nobody forgets why this matters to the patients upstairs.
Whatever we find, the record says what we can show.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: return with witnesses
interactions.body:
Hale reads the inspection authorization: staffing, the escorted route, radio contact, exit procedure.

Hale: Every person accounted for. Every exit checked.

Rahman: And nobody forgets why this matters to the patients upstairs.

You: What exactly are we trying to establish today?

Hale: Whether the independent observations can be repeated under the approved inspection procedure.

Facilities: If the conditions change, the operation stops. We don't continue because we're curious.

All three safeguards are mandatory: originals preserved, return procedure verified, clinical coverage confirmed.

options.label: "Preserve the original observations and record new findings independently."
options.response: Hale: Logged. New sheets, new notes, originals untouched.

options.label: "Verify the return procedure first."
options.response: Facilities: Return route walked and checked. Stop word is 'hold'.

options.label: "Confirm clinical coverage while we're away."
options.response: Rahman: I'm covering the ward. Nobody upstairs goes without.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: the team pass
interactions.body: Hale: If we get an answer, good. If we don't, we come back with everyone who went down.

options.label: Offer to go ahead alone and save the team the trip
options.response: Hale: No. Nobody goes down on their own.

options.label: Take the team pass and go down with the team
options.response: Team pass logged: ward entry, maintenance and the threshold, for this inspection only.

interactions.title: The room in two states
interactions.body:
Two recordings of the former treatment room's inner door, over what looks like the same interval. In one the door is shut. In the other it stands open.

You: Have the timestamps been reconciled?

Facilities: The clocks were checked, but I want the original timing records reviewed again.

Hale: Nobody opens that door to investigate.

options.label: Open the door to see which recording is right
options.response: Hale: No. We record it. We don't go in.

options.label: Record what differs before deciding what it means
options.response: Both recordings logged as they are, with their clock sources. The contradiction is preserved as an unresolved observation.

interactions.unavailable_body: Observation room records. Not part of this inspection.
interactions.completed_body: Two recordings, one door, two states. Preserved as unresolved; timing records under review.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: everyone back
interactions.body:
Hale counts the team in. Everyone who went down came back.

Hale: Recordings sealed for the analyst.

options.label: Ask to keep the pass for another look
options.response: Hale: No. The inspection is over. Any further entry needs its own approval.

options.label: Return the team pass and log everyone accounted for
options.response: Team pass returned. Ward entry, maintenance and threshold access withdrawn.

interactions.title: What the records were for
interactions.body:
The records historian's notes.

Historian: Some missing records are ordinary archival failures. Different numbering systems, incomplete transfers, boxes that were never indexed.

You: And the ones that don't fit the chronology?

Historian: Those remain unresolved. The mistake would be pretending they all have the same explanation.

options.label: Attribute all the gaps to one person in the hospital's past
options.response: Historian: There's no evidence for that. Some gaps are filing; some are unknown. One name for all of them would be invention.

options.label: Restore the timeline from authenticated records only
options.response: Timeline rebuilt from authenticated entries. Unauthenticated entries listed separately.

options.label: Flag every entry with unknown provenance
options.response: Unknown-provenance entries flagged, not removed.

options.label: Keep archival gaps separate from proven misconduct
options.response: Archival gaps and proven misconduct filed under separate headings. Nothing moved between them without evidence.

interactions.completed_body: Timeline from authenticated records; unknown provenance flagged; archival gaps kept apart from misconduct.

interactions.title: An evidence-based choice
interactions.body:
The independent analyst's report.

Analyst: We've verified the integrity of the files submitted for review. That doesn't establish every interpretation.

Hale: But there is a discrepancy.

Analyst: More than one. Some are explainable. Others remain unresolved.

Rahman: None of this should become part of a patient's psychiatric formulation simply because somebody complained about the same location.

You: We need two separate records: the clinical assessment and the environmental investigation.

options.label: "The cause is supernatural."
options.response: Analyst: I'd ask you to revise that. A conclusion about mechanism goes beyond what the official evidence establishes.

options.label: "Independent observations conflict with the established environmental record; mechanism undetermined."
options.response: Analyst: That's what the evidence supports.

options.label: "Preserve the discrepancy and pursue clearly bounded testing."
options.response: Analyst: Agreed. Bounded, documented, stoppable.

interactions.title: Naomi Bennett: not the basement
interactions.body:
Bennett: Doctor, I need you for something that doesn't involve the basement.

You: That sounds refreshing.

Bennett: A patient has questions about the plan, and we've got an outstanding follow-up before evening handoff.

options.label: Ask if it can wait until the review is finished
options.response: Bennett: It can't. The review doesn't get to decide when patients need us.

options.label: Take the questions, and hand the follow-up to the receiving team with a deadline
options.response:
Questions answered within your role; the follow-up handed to the receiving team with a named deadline before evening handoff.

Bennett: Everybody's talking about Ward Zero, but the patients still need people to show up for them.

You: That's why we're here.

Bennett: Good. Because the EHR still hasn't learned to write its own progress notes.

interactions.title: The four-source test
interactions.body:
Four files on the worksheet: original recordings, technical measurements, physical marker logs, and an exported summary.

Analyst: We can authenticate the recordings. We can verify the measurement procedure. We can also establish where some of the evidence shares a common source.

options.label: Count the four files as four independent sources
options.response: Analyst: The exported summary came from the same recordings. Counting it again would count one source twice.

options.label: Discount the shared-source copy before counting
options.response:
You: Which means we shouldn't count those records twice.

Analyst: Correct. After accounting for shared sources and known errors, the remaining observations still do not agree with the documented physical layout. A reproducible discrepancy our current technical review cannot explain.

Rahman: Then let's make sure that's how it's reported.

interactions.completed_body: Shared sources counted once. A reproducible discrepancy the technical review cannot explain; mechanism not asserted.

interactions.title: The decision nobody can make alone
interactions.body:
Voss: We've established that the observations remain inconsistent after independent review. We haven't established why.

Hale: Ward Zero stays restricted.

Rahman: Any operational changes must protect continuity of care.

Voss: What do we tell independent oversight, and what further investigation do we authorize?

Hale: You've been involved since the first transfer discrepancy. What's your recommendation?

options.label: Suggest waiting to report until there's an explanation
options.response: Voss: We cannot make uncertainty disappear by declining to document it.

options.label: Refer the authenticated findings to qualified external reviewers
options.response: Voss: Then we prepare a factual referral.

options.label: Maintain the restriction and preserve the evidence without another inspection
options.response: Hale: That's a defensible safety position.

options.label: Authorize a limited, accountable investigation with oversight and stop conditions
options.response: Rahman: As long as patient care and access controls are protected.

interactions.title: Mara Ellis: the people who stayed
interactions.body: Mara: I heard the hospital is still reviewing some old records. Does that mean my aunt's record is one of them?

options.label: Tell her the old records explain how she's been feeling
options.response: You stop yourself. Nothing in the building review says anything about Mara's health, and her assessment stands on its own.

options.label: "The discrepancy you raised remains part of the authorized historical review."
options.response:
You: I can't give you an explanation we haven't established.

Mara: I think what bothered me most was feeling like no one wanted to listen.

You: You deserved an assessment based on the information available, and an opportunity to explain your concerns.

Mara: I know I'm not always easy when I'm frustrated.

You: Frustration doesn't make your questions irrelevant.

options.label: Ask her what has bothered her most
options.response:
Mara: I think what bothered me most was feeling like no one wanted to listen.

You: You deserved an assessment based on the information available, and an opportunity to explain your concerns. The discrepancy you raised remains part of the authorized historical review. I can't give you an explanation we haven't established.

Mara: I know I'm not always easy when I'm frustrated.

You: Frustration doesn't make your questions irrelevant.

interactions.title: Independent review
interactions.body:
Voss signs the external referral. The originals stay here; the limitations are listed on the first page.

Voss: This may take longer than any of us would like.

options.label: "As long as the findings are preserved and the questions remain open."
options.response: Referral sent. Originals retained.

interactions.title: Restricted access
interactions.body:
The old entrance is sealed under documented restrictions, with a periodic review date.

Hale: Nobody enters without authorization.

options.label: "And the records?"
options.response: Hale: Preserved. Closing a door doesn't mean pretending nothing happened.

interactions.title: Continuing inquiry
interactions.body:
An accountable review goes ahead: oversight, limited access, defined stop conditions.

Rahman: What happens if the next review still doesn't answer everything?

options.label: "Then we document what remains unknown and decide whether further testing is justified."
options.response: Rahman: Uncertainty isn't permission to abandon our standards.

interactions.title: The next patient
interactions.body: Bennett: Morning, Doctor. Ready for rounds?

options.label: "Who are we seeing first?"
options.response: Bennett: Whoever needs us.

sign_out.title: Clinical handoff
sign_out.undocumented_message: Outstanding clinical review still requires an appropriate handoff.

campaign_end.title: Ashcroft State Forensic Hospital: end of the main campaign

lines.text: The authenticated findings went to qualified external reviewers, with the originals preserved.
Ward Zero is sealed under documented restriction, with its evidence preserved and a periodic review.
A limited, accountable inquiry continues under independent oversight and stop conditions.
The corridor repetition stays on record as observed and unverified.
After shared sources were counted once, a reproducible discrepancy remains unexplained.
Mara's questions were heard, and her care stayed her own.
Patient care never waited on the investigation.
